Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — tokens/sec profile and headroom

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked promising. We are moving toward a 3-month pilot and need a clear sizing recommendation for a dedicated capacity commit that meets our SLOs. Specifically:

- Target p50 latency: <= 120ms for conversational prompts (avg length ~280 tokens)
- Peak sustained TPS (inference requests/sec): around 55 requests/sec with typical batching
- Token distribution: 60% short (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (>512)

Can Redwood produce a tokens/sec estimate (tokens/sec delivery) mapping to GPU counts for your recommended instance types, plus expected headroom before SLA degradation? We need this for procurement and to justify the commit internally.

I've attached our SLA requirements doc and a CSV of sample request profiles. Happy to jump on a short call but getting the numbers in writing will speed procurement.

Best,
Emma

Emma / team —

Attached is a preliminary sizing workbook (kw_dedicated_sizing_summary.xlsx) and a CSV export of the token profile we used. Key takeaways (preliminary):

- Baseline model: open-llm-3b-optimized (quantized int8 recommended for cost/headroom tradeoff)
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv (under your distribution, continuous load):
  * p50 latency <=120ms: ~92K tokens/sec per GPU (approx, assumes batching avg 1.8 reqs/batch)
  * p95 latency ~180ms: ~115K tokens/sec per GPU (latency increases non linear at saturation)

- Mapping to request TPS (using your 280-token avg):
  * Tokens/sec 92K -> ~328 requests/sec capacity per GPU (p50)
  * For your stated peak sustained 55 req/sec => 55 / 328 = 0.168 GPUs required nominally

- Recommended committed sizing (to meet p50 <=120ms with 1.2x headroom):
  * Minimum commit: 1 GPU (gives ~5.9x headroom vs peak) — we recommend 2 GPUs for redundancy and to cover uneven load distributions and maintenance windows

- Sensitivity/notes:
  * If you add function-calling/long-form generation spikes (long tail >1024 tokens), effective tokens/sec drops ~30% for those periods — plan burst policies accordingly.
  * Quantization to int4 (experimental) can improve throughput by ~20-30% but requires quality validation.
  * Autoscale/Burst: configure burst pool at +2 GPUs with regional fallback to avoid SLA violations during sustained >3x expected peak.

I've included quick screenshot tables in the workbook and a tab showing how different batch sizes and kv-cache hit rates affect tokens/sec. Priyom, please add the monthly token burn forecast and cost estimate to the pricing tab.

Attachments: kw_dedicated_sizing_summary.xlsx, kw_token_profile.csv

Thanks,
